title: The Warning
briefing: Credible intelligence indicates an imminent AI-enabled attack on UK infrastructure. The source has been right before and wrong before. There is no time to commission analysis, and the advice in the room is not agreed.

forecast.question: Chance the intelligence is right and an attack is attempted.

briefingSignal.leansTrue: Late read, low confidence: a second channel reports matching preparations. The warning may be sound.
briefingSignal.leansFalse: Late read, low confidence: no second channel corroborates the report. The warning may be mistaken.

shah.stance: A single source with a mixed record. Prepare quietly; do not spend credibility you will need for a real one.

harcourt.stance: If it is real and we did nothing, there is no explaining that afterwards. Warn operators and shut down what is exposed.

chen.stance: A precautionary shutdown costs the economy the same whether or not anything was coming.

okafor.stance: Cry wolf once and the next warning is ignored. Raise the standards, which helps either way.

choices.text: Hold the intelligence closely and prepare under existing law.
choices.headline: No public statement is made; operators are briefed in confidence.
Emergency agent security standards are imposed, citing an unspecified threat.

choices.text: Public warning and precautionary shutdown of exposed services.
choices.headline: Government issues a public warning and shuts down exposed services as a precaution.

choices.text: Task the government incident-response model to test the intelligence.
choices.headline: The government's incident-response model sweeps exposed networks overnight.

evidencePanel.known: The UK's official assessment is that AI will raise the frequency and intensity of intrusions.
evidencePanel.unknown: Whether this warning is one of them. Players sometimes prepare for nothing, and that is part of the lesson.
evidencePanel.whyItMatters: Acting on a false alarm costs credibility. Ignoring a true one costs far more. You must choose before you know which this is.

sources.label: NCSC, Impact of AI on cyber threat from now to 2027
